newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns six Saudi banks public info ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns six Saudi banks public info ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's on Tuesday assigned public information ratings to six Saudi banks and said the strong financial profile of individual banks in the Saudi system contrasted with an economy vulnerable to oil price moves and an unfavourable legal system.
S&P said it rated Saudi American Bank, Saudi British Bank, Al Bank Al Saudi Al Fransi, Riyad Bank and Arab National Bank were all rated BBBpi, while National Commercial Bank was rated BBpi.

"Saudi banks have strong financial profiles by international comparison," S&P said in a statement. "Their healthy profitability derives largely from their balance sheet structures, which benefit from a high amount of non-remunerated deposits (about one quarter of total footings)."

"Moreover, given their large customer deposit base, almost twice the size of their loan portfolios, Saudi banks are very liquid," it added. S&P said the banks were also well capitalised as equity-to-loans ratios averaged 28 percent for the sector.
"It would take an enormous downturn in the market before their solvency were threatened."
But S&P said Saudi banks faced the challenge of operating in a volatile economy that was clearly sensitive to the price of oil.

"This sensitivity to oil prices can lead to big swings in government revenues. Since the government is the main driver of the economy, when its revenues drop the economy slumps, which happened in the 1994-95 period," it said.
S&P said Saudi American Bank was 30 percent owned by Citibank, Saudi British Bank was 40 percent owned by HSBC Holdings, and Al Bank Al Saudi Al Fransi was 30 percent owned by Banque Indosuez.
